text:
Marathon Petroleum shares fell barely at all today (down 0.04%), but the stock has lost nearly 6% over the past two weeks after peaking at $414.65 on November 13th. The decline follows geopolitical tension in the Middle East—Iran escalated military threats as a third U.S. carrier arrived in the Gulf on November 17th—which typically weighs on energy stocks despite the initial risk premium. Oil prices remain relatively stable (U.S. crude at $89.62/barrel), but refiners like Marathon are sensitive to uncertainty about supply disruptions that could reshape margins.

The broader picture shows refineries are running at high capacity (95.2%) with ample crude and product inventories, which limits upside for processors when crude prices aren't spiking and demand signals remain mixed. Rising heating oil prices (up 59% year-over-year) suggest winter demand could strengthen, but that benefit may already be priced in after the sharp two-week drop.
